svg.title: GoTavern vs SillyTavern (Node) - paired benchmark, ubuntu26
svg.desc: Cold start to first /version 200: SillyTavern 12,985 ms, GoTavern 136 ms (95.48x faster); Steady-state memory (RSS): SillyTavern 925.8 MB, GoTavern 37.0 MB (25.04x lighter); GET /version latency: SillyTavern 34.05 ms, GoTavern 0.422 ms (80.61x faster); GET / latency (HTML shell): SillyTavern 12.18 ms, GoTavern 1.67 ms (7.29x faster). For timing panels a lower value is faster; for memory a lower value is lighter. Degree of improvement is per panel, each drawn against its own zero-based axis. Methodology and provenance are stated in the README section below the figure.
svg.text: Measured against pinned SillyTavern on the same machine, in the same run, in alternating rounds.
Runner ubuntu26 - 3 rounds x 30 sequential requests per path - medians shown
Each panel says what the difference means: faster for timing, lighter for memory.
median of 3 rounds; empty data root, no config.yaml
VmRSS from /proc, sampled after readiness and after 60 requests; median of 6
median of 90 sequential requests, same client both subjects
median of 90 sequential requests, body fully consumed
Every bar is drawn against its own panel's zero-based axis, whose maximum is printed on the panel. No axis is truncated and no ratio replaces a value.
Ratios are computed from the two printed values in each panel; they are a restatement, not a separate measurement.
SillyTavern 1.19.0 (pinned commit 06bde939) vs GoTavern at a3c2f53 - same checkout, same data-root seeding, same port allocator.
Workflow: GoTavern smoke metrics, run 40898332226 - shared GitHub runner, so these are runner-dependent numbers, not a budget.
Full methodology and provenance: README, "Performance" section.
